The fix can be copied as is with the names changed.

fix.subject: drivers: sensor: fix thread function signatures

evidence: Commit 191865b5 ("Fix thread function signatures to avoid stack corruption on thread exit") changed lps22hh_thread from taking a struct lps22hh_data pointer to the k_thread_entry_t form (void *p1, void *p2, void *p3) and dropped the (k_thread_entry_t) cast at k_thread_create; lps22hh_trigger.c still has that form (lines 126 and 194). lps2xdf_trigger.c, an ST trigger file built the same way, still has the pre-fix pattern: `static void lps2xdf_thread(struct lps2xdf_data *lps2xdf)` at line 76 and `(k_thread_entry_t)lps2xdf_thread, lps2xdf,` at line 142, while k_thread_entry_t is `void (*)(void *p1, void *p2, void *p3)` (include/zephyr/arch/arch_interface.h:46), so the thread is started through a function pointer of a different type. Nothing in the LPS2XDF driver handles this another way, and the fix only needs ARG_UNUSED and a local pointer assigned from p1, which are available. The runtime effect is small: the code is only built with the non-default LPS2XDF_TRIGGER_OWN_THREAD option (the default is the global thread), and the thread body is `while (1)` and never returns, so the "thread exit" case named in the commit cannot occur here; what remains is a call through a mismatched function type, which C leaves undefined.
impact_note: The thread loops forever and never returns, so the stack corruption on thread exit that the commit names cannot happen here; only the formally undefined call through a mismatched function type remains, and only with the non-default own-thread trigger mode.

title: The Kinetis UART driver reconfigures the UART at run time without waiting for the last byte to finish sending.
summary: In June 2026 the NXP LPUART driver (uart_mcux_lpuart.c) started waiting for the Transmission Complete flag before uart_configure() reconfigures the port, and later bounded that wait to 300 ms with -EBUSY, so that a byte still being sent is not cut off. The Kinetis UART driver uart_mcux.c still calls UART_Init with the new settings immediately in uart_mcux_configure, with no check of kUART_TransmissionCompleteFlag, even though the driver already reads that flag elsewhere. If an application changes baud rate or framing right after writing data, the last byte will likely go out truncated or garbled. What is missing to be certain: the body of UART_Init is in the NXP SDK, outside this repository, and the original report covered LPUART only; when porting, the wait belongs only on the runtime path because the same function also runs at boot from uart_mcux_init.

fix.subject: drivers: serial: uart_mcux_lpuart: ensure TX completes before reconfig

evidence: Per the commit message, the fix adds "a wait for the Transmission Complete (TC) flag at the start of mcux_lpuart_configure()" because "uart_configure() could interrupt an ongoing transmission, causing the last byte to not be fully sent on the UART bus"; the LPUART driver still has it at the pinned commit, now bounded with WAIT_FOR on LPUART_STAT_TC_MASK. In uart_mcux.c, uart_mcux_configure is the runtime .configure callback and, like the pre-fix LPUART function, goes straight to re-initialization (UART_Init with the new baud rate and TX/RX enabled) without checking kUART_TransmissionCompleteFlag. The status bit the fix needs exists here: uart_mcux_irq_tx_complete already reads kUART_TransmissionCompleteFlag, while poll_out and fifo_fill only wait for kUART_TxDataRegEmptyFlag, so a byte can still be shifting out when configure is called; the sibling NXP driver uart_mcux_flexcomm.c guards the same step ("Wait for USART to finish transmission and turn off"). Confidence is medium because the body of UART_Init is in the NXP SDK, not in this repository, so it cannot be confirmed here whether it disables the transmitter or reprograms the baud rate mid-frame, and the commit reports the behaviour only "on NXP LPUART". The same function is also called from uart_mcux_init at boot, so the wait has to be added on the runtime path only.

evidence_refs.quote: /* Wait for USART to finish transmission and turn off */

title: The legacy Infineon UART driver's TX abort always reports 0 bytes sent, and sends no abort event at all if reading the DMA status fails.
summary: On 2026-11-05 the Infineon PDL UART driver (uart_infineon_pdl.c) changed its async TX abort to report how many bytes were actually sent (buffer length minus the DMA's pending length) and to still deliver UART_TX_ABORTED when reading the DMA status fails. The legacy-HAL driver uart_infineon.c, built when USE_INFINEON_LEGACY_HAL is set, has the same abort function with the old code: it always reports a length of 0, and on a status-read error it returns without sending the event. An application that aborts a transfer, or whose transfer hits the TX timeout, is therefore told that nothing was sent even when part of the buffer already went out, which can lead to resending or losing track of data. The status-read error is probably rare, because the paired DMA driver's get_status fails only for an invalid channel, so the wrong length is the main practical effect.

fix.subject: drivers: serial: uart_infineon_pdl: fix async UART correctness issues

evidence: The picked hunk changes the PDL driver's ifx_cat1_uart_async_tx_abort() so that UART_TX_ABORTED carries buf_len - stat.pending_length instead of a fixed 0, and so that a dma_get_status() failure still delivers the event (with length 0) instead of jumping to unlock; the commit message calls this "report actual transferred length when aborting TX". uart_infineon.c (the legacy-HAL driver for the same infineon,uart compatible) has the same function with the pre-fix code: when dma_get_status() fails it logs "Error stopping Tx DMA" and does goto unlock, skipping the event, and otherwise it always sets evt.data.tx.len = 0; the TX timeout work calls this same function. Zephyr's UART API states that after uart_tx_abort "#UART_TX_ABORTED event will be generated with amount of data sent" and documents uart_event_tx.len as the "Number of bytes sent". Everything the fix needs exists on this side: dma_tx.buf_len is set in ifx_cat1_uart_async_tx(), the file already computes buf_len - stat.pending_length for RX from dma_get_status(), and the paired legacy DMA driver (dma_infineon.c) fills pending_length; nothing else in uart_infineon.c reports a transmitted count for an abort (dma_transmitted_bytes is only reset). The commit's other changes (NULL guards, arming the timeout only with flow control) are outside the picked hunk and are not judged here.

evidence_refs.quote: #UART_TX_ABORTED event will be generated with amount of data sent.

title: ADXL355 streaming can stall after an interrupt arrives while no stream request is pending, because the re-arm flag is never cleared.
summary: On 2026-10-29 the ADXL372 driver was fixed to clear its FIFO-interrupt flag when an interrupt arrives with no stream request pending, so that the next stream request flushes and reconfigures the FIFO; the ADXL345 driver already did the same. The ADXL355 stream code follows the same template but still returns from adxl355_stream_irq_handler() and adxl355_process_status1_cb() without clearing data->fifo_watermark_irq. If the FIFO fills after a stream is cancelled or between requests, the next stream with the same trigger skips the flush and only waits for a new edge on the interrupt pin, so the new stream may never receive data. The fix is one assignment in each of the two early returns. Whether the ADXL355 interrupt line really stays asserted in this state is not stated in the repository and would need a hardware check.

fix.subject: drivers: sensor: adxl372: re-arm stream after an orphaned interrupt

evidence: adxl355_stream.c is built the same way as the pre-fix ADXL372 code: adxl355_submit_stream() reprograms INT_MAP and flushes the FIFO (adxl355_flush_fifo(), then a STATUS read) only when fifo_watermark_irq differs from data->fifo_watermark_irq, and then arms the GPIO with GPIO_INT_EDGE_TO_ACTIVE. adxl355_gpio_callback() disables the GPIO interrupt and calls adxl355_stream_irq_handler(), and both that handler (line 377) and adxl355_process_status1_cb() (line 259) simply return when data->sqe == NULL without resetting data->fifo_watermark_irq; no other code in the driver resets that flag. So after a stream is cancelled or between requests, an interrupt with no pending request leaves the FIFO untouched, and the next submit with the same trigger skips the flush and only re-arms an edge interrupt, which is the failure the commit message describes as "INT1 stays high and the new stream never gets an edge". The fix needs only the existing fifo_watermark_irq field (adxl355.h), so it carries over as one assignment in each early return. Confidence is medium because whether the ADXL355 interrupt line stays asserted until the FIFO is flushed is a hardware property the repository does not state, although the driver itself re-enables the interrupt only after a flush in adxl355_flush_rtio().
same_problem_note: Same unfixed code in adxl355_stream.c as zephyr-102: both fixes make a driver clear fifo_watermark_irq when an interrupt arrives with no pending stream request (ADXL345 on 2026-08-03, ADXL372 on 2026-10-29).

title: MAX30009 streaming can stall after an interrupt arrives while no stream request is pending, because the re-arm flag is never cleared.
summary: On 2026-10-29 the ADXL372 driver was fixed to clear its FIFO-interrupt flag when an interrupt arrives with no stream request pending, so that the next stream request flushes the FIFO and re-reads the status; the ADXL345 driver already did the same. The MAX30009 stream code, written from the same template, still returns from max30009_stream_irq_handler() and max30009_process_status1_cb() without clearing data->fifo_watermark_irq. If the FIFO reaches its threshold after a stream is cancelled or between requests, the next stream with the same trigger skips the flush and the STATUS1 read and only waits for a new edge on the interrupt pin, so the new stream may never receive data. The fix is one assignment in each of the two early returns. Whether the MAX30009 interrupt output really stays asserted in this state is not stated in the repository and would need a hardware check.

fix.subject: drivers: sensor: adxl372: re-arm stream after an orphaned interrupt

evidence: max30009_stream.c follows the same pattern as the pre-fix ADXL372 code: max30009_submit_stream() updates A_FULL_EN, flushes the FIFO (max30009_flush_dev()) and reads STATUS1 only when fifo_watermark_irq differs from data->fifo_watermark_irq, and then arms the GPIO with GPIO_INT_EDGE_TO_ACTIVE. max30009_gpio_callback() disables the GPIO interrupt and calls max30009_stream_irq_handler(), and both that handler (line 418) and max30009_process_status1_cb() (line 280) return when data->sqe == NULL without resetting data->fifo_watermark_irq; nothing else in the driver resets that flag. With the default MAX30009_TRIGGER_NONE no trigger thread runs either, so after an interrupt with no pending stream nothing reads STATUS1 (the step the trigger code labels "Clear the status") or drains the FIFO, and the next submit with the same trigger skips the flush and only waits for a new edge, the failure the commit message describes for ADXL372 ("INT1 stays high and the new stream never gets an edge"). The fix needs only the existing fifo_watermark_irq field (max30009.h), so it carries over as one assignment in each early return. Confidence is medium because whether the MAX30009 interrupt output stays asserted until STATUS1 is read or the FIFO is flushed is a hardware property the repository does not state.
same_problem_note: Same unfixed code in max30009_stream.c as zephyr-104: both fixes make a driver clear fifo_watermark_irq when an interrupt arrives with no pending stream request (ADXL345 on 2026-08-03, ADXL372 on 2026-10-29).

title: The LSM6DSL driver rejects any requested sampling rate that is not exactly one of its table values, instead of rounding up to the next supported rate as the ISM330DHCX driver now does.
summary: In 2024 the ISM330DHCX driver changed its rate lookup from an exact match to the first supported rate at or above the request (commit 50ad2e05), and the same author made the same change in IIS2ICLX. The LSM6DSL driver still uses the exact match in lsm6dsl_freq_to_odr_val, so setting SENSOR_ATTR_SAMPLING_FREQUENCY to a value outside its table returns -EINVAL and the sensor keeps its old rate. The change has to be adapted rather than copied, because the LSM6DSL table puts the 1.6 Hz entry last and the same function restores the saved rate on PM resume, so a request or saved value of 1 must still map to index 11. It is not certain that maintainers regard exact matching as a bug in this driver rather than a deliberate API choice.

fix.subject: drivers/sensor/st: ism330dhcx: fix odr setting

evidence: The hunk turns ism330dhcx_freq_to_odr_val from an exact match into picking the first table rate at or above the request; the commit message says "Loop inside the odr array until we find the first value which is "<=" (amd not "==") the argument", and the same author's matching iis2iclx commit c6f8d37056 states the intent: "Do not fail when requested rate passed in SENSOR_ATTR_SAMPLING_FREQUENCY is not matching any of the odr values supported by sensor. Instead, round it up to the next one." lsm6dsl_freq_to_odr_val (line 32) is the same lookup with the pre-fix exact test at line 37, and lsm6dsl_accel_odr_set / lsm6dsl_gyro_odr_set pass val->val1 straight to it and return its -EINVAL, so any rate that is not exactly a table value (for example 100 Hz) is rejected; nothing else in the driver rounds the request. The fix cannot be copied verbatim: the lsm6dsl table ends with 1 (index 11, documented as 1.6Hz in Kconfig), so it is not ascending, and the same function maps the saved rate back to an index on PM resume (line 856), so a plain <= would turn 1 Hz into 12.5 Hz. Confidence is low because exact matching in this older driver could be read as a deliberate API choice rather than a defect.

title: The STM32 DFSDM microphone driver clamps 24-bit samples against an unsigned -BIT(23) bound, so in interrupt mode every 24-bit sample comes out as full-scale positive or negative.
summary: In September 2026 the STM32 MDF microphone driver replaced the 24-bit clamp bounds -BIT(23) and BIT(23) - 1 with signed constants, because the unsigned BIT() made the lower bound wrap to a huge positive number and turned recordings into a full-scale square wave. The STM32 DFSDM microphone driver has the same write-sample helper with the identical clamp line and still uses the unsigned bounds. When it is configured for 17 to 24-bit samples without DMA, each non-negative sample is written as -8388608 and each small negative sample as 8388607, so the recorded audio is lost. Defining signed 24-bit limits as the MDF driver did fixes it.

fix.subject: drivers: audio: dmic_stm32_mdf: fix the clamp on 24-bit samples

evidence: The MDF fix replaces CLAMP(sample, -BIT(23), BIT(23) - 1) with signed limits because, in the commit's words, "BIT() has an unsigned type, so -BIT(23) is evaluated using unsigned arithmetic and wraps to a large positive value instead of producing -8388608. As a result, the bounds passed to CLAMP() are invalid", which on hardware gave "a full-scale square wave at pcm_width 24". dmic_stm32_dfsdm_write_sample (line 133) is the same helper with the same int32_t sample and the identical pre-fix line 143; BIT is (1UL << (n)) in util_macro.h and CLAMP compares val against low first (util.h line 531), so every non-negative sample is clamped to the wrapped low bound and small negative samples to the high bound. The 24-bit case is reachable: sample_size is DIV_ROUND_UP(pcm_width, 8) (line 168), configure accepts pcm_width up to DFSDM_DATA_RES = 24 (lines 50, 755), and without a DMA channel the driver runs HAL_DFSDM_FilterRegularStart_IT (line 515), whose conversion callback writes each sample through this helper. Nothing in the DFSDM driver defines signed 24-bit limits or otherwise avoids the wrap; only the DMA path, which does not use this helper, is unaffected.

evidence_refs.quote: static void dmic_stm32_dfsdm_write_sample(uint8_t *dst, uint8_t sample_size, int32_t sample)

title: The ICM566xx driver converts the APEX pedometer cadence with the old formula, which reports a wrong step rate and divides by zero before the first step.
summary: In 2026 the ICM45686 and ICM42x70 drivers corrected their pedometer cadence conversion: the u6.2 raw value is now divided as is, and a raw value of 0 reports 0 steps/s instead of dividing by zero. The ICM566xx driver, added with a copy of the same helper, still divides by raw_val + (raw_val & 0x03), so any cadence with non-zero fractional bits comes out too low. Reading the pedometer channel before the sensor has reported a step passes a cadence of 0 and divides by zero. The fixed function can be copied over with only the name changed.

fix.subject: drivers: sensor: tdk: fix APEX pedometer cadence conversion

evidence: The fix rewrites the APEX pedometer cadence conversion because, per the commit message, "The cadence value is in u6.2 format, so the number of samples between two steps is raw_val / 4, but the conversion divided by raw_val + (raw_val & 0x03), double-counting the fractional bits and dividing by zero when no cadence had been reported yet." icm566xx_apex_pedometer_cadence_convert (line 145) is the same function with the same uint8_t raw_val and dmp_odr_hz parameters, the same "Converting u6.2" comment (line 150) and the identical pre-fix formula at line 151. It is called the same way: in pedometer mode the SENSOR_CHAN_APEX_MOTION read in icm566xx.c (line 440) passes data->pedometer_cadence, which is only written from ped_data.step_cadence after a step-detect event (apex line 117) and otherwise keeps its zero initial value in the static device data (icm566xx.c line 815), with dmp_odr_hz set to 50 (apex line 163). So the ICM566xx driver both miscomputes the cadence whenever the two fractional bits are non-zero and divides by zero if the channel is read before the first step; it has no guard elsewhere, and the fix needs nothing beyond the function's own arguments.

title: The MAX32 RTIO I2C driver never completes a zero-length transfer whose address is ACKed, so "i2c scan" and any other 0-length write hang forever.
summary: Commit 7ae44ec850 (2025-04) fixed i2c_max32.c so that its controller ISR releases the waiting thread when a target ACKs its address and the message carries no data, which stopped "i2c scan" from looping forever in interrupt mode. The RTIO variant i2c_max32_rtio.c, built instead of i2c_max32.c when CONFIG_I2C_RTIO is enabled, still has the old ADDR_ACK branch, and none of its other completion paths fire for a message with no data, so such a transfer is never completed. The caller then blocks forever in rtio_submit() while holding the bus lock, so the scan stops at the first device that answers and every later transfer on that I2C controller also blocks. The port has to be adapted: the RTIO driver signals completion with complete_flag and max32_complete() instead of a semaphore, and probably needs to issue the STOP itself. Separately, max32_complete() already returns without completing anything when the bus runs at the standard-speed clock setting (line 319), so this gap is what blocks the scan at the other speeds; none of this has been confirmed on hardware.

fix.subject: drivers: i2c: i2c_max32.c: Fix handling of 0-length I2C scan transactions

evidence: The picked hunk adds an else-branch to the ADDR_ACK case of i2c_max32_isr_controller() in i2c_max32.c that gives the xfer semaphore when tx_len == rx_len == 0; the commit message says such 0-length transactions, sent by "i2c scan", were "not being handled both by the Async i2c_max32_transfer and by the controller ISR" and caused "an infinite loop when CONFIG_I2C_MAX32_INTERRUPT is enabled". i2c_max32_rtio.c, which drivers/i2c/CMakeLists.txt builds instead of i2c_max32.c when CONFIG_I2C_RTIO is set, has the same controller ISR with the unchanged pre-fix ADDR_ACK branch (lines 206-214, which only enables TX_THD or RX_THD|DONE when there is data left), and max32_msg_start() starts a 0-length write the same way (tx_len = buf_len, ERR and ADDR_ACK interrupts, START plus the address byte). In this ISR the only ways to finish a message are the ERR path, the TX path guarded by req->tx_len (line 216), and the RX path, each leading to complete_flag == 1 (line 266) and max32_complete(); an ACKed 0-length write such as the shell scan's (i2c_shell.c line 76) therefore never completes, and i2c_rtio_transfer() waits forever in rtio_submit(r, 1) (i2c_rtio.c line 184) while holding ctx->lock (line 173). The RTIO driver has no xfer semaphore, so the fix must be adapted to signal completion through complete_flag/max32_complete(); the commit's second change (skip the BUSY wait) has no counterpart because the RTIO path does not busy-wait.

title: The Realtek Bee UART driver does not clear the other API's callback when one is set, so the interrupt-driven and async callbacks can both stay active even though exclusive callbacks are enabled by default.
summary: In 2022 commit 9f02eead added CONFIG_UART_EXCLUSIVE_API_CALLBACKS (default y when both the interrupt-driven and async APIs are enabled) and changed drivers such as uart_stm32.c so that setting the IRQ callback clears the async callback and vice versa. The Realtek Bee driver received its async API in August 2026 (eb525902e0) with the same field names (user_cb/user_data, async_cb/async_user_data), but uart_bee_irq_callback_set() and uart_bee_async_callback_set() still only store the new callback. Because uart_bee_isr() calls the interrupt-driven callback on every UART interrupt before handling async RX idle, a callback installed earlier (for example by a console or shell) keeps running during async transfers and can read or react to data meant for the DMA receiver, against the documented Kconfig behaviour. The problem only shows when both APIs are used on the same UART instance; the four-line #if CONFIG_UART_EXCLUSIVE_API_CALLBACKS blocks from uart_stm32.c can be copied as is.

fix.subject: serial: allow callback setting to be exclusive

evidence: The fix makes the two callback setters exclusive because, per the commit, "having callbacks on both API would interfere with each other in almost all cases"; the CONFIG_UART_EXCLUSIVE_API_CALLBACKS option it adds (still present, default y, depends on UART_ASYNC_API && UART_INTERRUPT_DRIVEN) documents that "calling uart_callback_set() would disable the callback previously set via uart_irq_callback_set()". uart_bee.c implements both APIs (Kconfig.bee selects SERIAL_SUPPORT_INTERRUPT and SERIAL_SUPPORT_ASYNC, the API table has both .irq_callback_set and .callback_set) and uses the very same field names as uart_stm32.c, but uart_bee_irq_callback_set() (lines 432-433) and uart_bee_async_callback_set() (lines 494-495) only store their own callback, and nothing else in the file ever clears user_cb or async_cb. Its ISR has the same shape as the pre-fix STM32 one: uart_bee_isr() calls data->user_cb whenever it is set and then runs the async RX-idle handling, so a leftover interrupt-driven callback keeps running during async transfers. The generic wrappers in include/zephyr/drivers/uart/uart_internal.h just forward to the driver, so nothing outside the driver enforces exclusivity; maintainers still treat the omission as a defect (2026 commit 1718448d76 "silabs_eusart: Respect exclusive API callbacks").

title: The dummy display driver bounds horizontal writes by the buffer pitch instead of the written width, so it rejects valid partial-screen writes.
summary: In April 2024 the SDL display driver (commit acc2b51959) changed its write bounds check from `x + desc->pitch` to `x + desc->width`, because pitch is the row stride of the source buffer and a partial update taken from a full-screen buffer keeps pitch equal to the screen width. dummy_display_write in drivers/display/display_dummy.c still has the identical pre-fix assert and -EINVAL check. Any write with x > 0 from a buffer whose pitch is the full screen width therefore fails with -EINVAL, or trips the assertion when CONFIG_ASSERT is on, even though the area fits on the screen. Since the dummy display renders nothing, only applications and tests running against it see the spurious error; the fix is the same two-word change as in SDL.

fix.subject: drivers: display: sdl: Fix asserts in sdl_display_write

evidence: The SDL fix replaces `x + desc->pitch` with `x + desc->width` in both the horizontal-bound assert and the -EINVAL check of sdl_display_write; the commit message says "We expect to be able to update a portion of the display from a portion of the buffer, in which case pitch must remain the screen width. Expecting x + pitch to be smaller than the screen width is incorrect." The display API defines pitch as the "Number of pixels between consecutive rows in the data buffer", so it says nothing about where the written area ends on screen. dummy_display_write in display_dummy.c (lines 46 and 52) has the identical pre-fix assert and check, in the same order and with the same messages as the SDL code before the fix, and the function then just returns 0. Nothing in the dummy driver depends on hardware or configuration that would make the pitch-based bound correct there: its config holds only width and height and it accepts the same display_buffer_descriptor. A write at x > 0 from a buffer whose pitch is the full screen width is therefore rejected with -EINVAL (or trips the assert with CONFIG_ASSERT) even though the written area fits.

evidence_refs.quote: static int dummy_display_write(const struct device *dev, const uint16_t x,
Enable dummy display driver compliant with display driver API.
/** Number of pixels between consecutive rows in the data buffer */

impact_note: The dummy display draws nothing and only stands in for a real panel, so the effect is a spurious -EINVAL or assertion for code and tests running against it, not wrong output on hardware.

title: The HMC5883L driver asserts that sample_fetch is only called with SENSOR_CHAN_ALL, so a fetch of SENSOR_CHAN_MAGN_XYZ trips the assertion.
summary: In February 2025 the LIS3MDL magnetometer driver (commit b6604f160c) relaxed its sample_fetch assertion to accept SENSOR_CHAN_MAGN_XYZ as well as SENSOR_CHAN_ALL, because a data-ready handler that calls sensor_sample_fetch_chan(dev, trig->chan) with a MAGN_XYZ trigger crashed on the assertion. The HMC5883L magnetometer driver still has the identical `__ASSERT_NO_MSG(chan == SENSOR_CHAN_ALL);` in front of a read that fetches all three axes anyway, and it supports MAGN_XYZ in channel_get and passes the caller's trigger back to the handler. With CONFIG_ASSERT enabled, an application that fetches the MAGN_XYZ channel (for example from a data-ready trigger set on that channel) stops on the assertion. Release builds without assertions are unaffected, so this is a debug-build problem fixed by the same one-line change.

fix.subject: drivers/sensor: lis3mdl: fix lis3mdl_sample_fetch API

evidence: The lis3mdl fix widens the sample_fetch assertion from `chan == SENSOR_CHAN_ALL` to also accept SENSOR_CHAN_MAGN_XYZ; the commit message says it fixes "a runtime bug when both CONFIG_LIS3MDL_TRIGGER and CONFIG_ASSERT are set. The correct assertion should verify that sensor channel is either SENSOR_CHAN_ALL or SENSOR_CHAN_MAGN_XYZ." (the in-tree x_nucleo_iks01a1 sample sets `trig.chan = SENSOR_CHAN_MAGN_XYZ` and calls `sensor_sample_fetch_chan(dev, trig->chan)` from its data-ready handler). hmc5883l_sample_fetch has the identical pre-fix line `__ASSERT_NO_MSG(chan == SENSOR_CHAN_ALL);` followed by an unconditional burst read of all three axes, exactly like lis3mdl_sample_fetch, and its channel_get supports SENSOR_CHAN_MAGN_XYZ. The hmc5883l trigger code also hands the caller's own trigger back to the data-ready handler, so the same handler pattern reaches the assertion. Nothing hardware- or configuration-specific separates the two: the fix only uses the generic SENSOR_CHAN_MAGN_XYZ enum, and hmc5883l does not handle the channel anywhere else in sample_fetch.
impact_note: Only builds with CONFIG_ASSERT enabled are affected, where a valid MAGN_XYZ fetch halts on the assertion; without assertions the function already reads all three axes and behaves correctly.

title: The ENE KB1200 GPIO driver's port_set_masked_raw only ORs bits into the output register, so it can never drive a masked pin low.
summary: In July 2026 the ENE KB106x GPIO driver (commit b6b79411bc) fixed port_set_masked_raw to clear the masked bits before setting them, added a spinlock around output and interrupt register updates, masked ISR pending flags with the interrupt-enable register and cleared them before running callbacks. The older KB1200 GPIO driver from the same vendor still has the pre-fix `GPIOD |= (value & mask)`, so gpio_port_set_masked_raw (and gpio_port_set_masked) can raise pins but never lower them, and pins keep a stale high level. Its ISR and interrupt-configure code also keep the pre-fix pattern of firing callbacks for unmasked pending flags and clearing the write-1-to-clear pending register with read-modify-write, which can drop events that arrive meanwhile. The output-register fix can be copied directly, while the interrupt changes need to be rewritten for KB1200's differently structured function, and the wake-mask change to get_pending_int does not apply because KB1200 has no wake support in its driver.

fix.subject: drivers: gpio: kb106x: GPIO api bugs fix

evidence: The kb106x commit ("Fix gpio_port_set_masked_raw api bug" and "Fix gpio_pin_interrupt_configure race condition bug") replaces `GPIOD |= (value & mask)` with `GPIOD = (GPIOD & ~mask) | (value & mask)` under a spinlock; kb1200_gpio_port_set_masked_raw still has the identical pre-fix line (107), so a masked pin whose value bit is 0 is never driven low, although the GPIO API says writing value 0 sets a low level and the kb1200 GPIOD is the same "Output Data Register". The ISR hunk also applies: gpio_kb1200_isr reads GPTDPF without masking by GPTDIE and clears it only after the callbacks, with `GPTDPF |= pending_flag`, which (given the driver's own write-1 "clear pending flag" usage) also clears flags that arrived during the callbacks; the kb1200 gptd.h has the same GPTDIE/GPTDPF layout as kb106x. The interrupt-configure hunk applies in adapted form: kb1200 reprograms the trigger while GPTDIE may still be set and clears the pending flag with WRITE_BIT (line 172), whose `|=` writes back every pending bit, which is the pattern the fix replaced with `GPTDPF = BIT(pin)`, but the function is structured differently (enable/disable inside if/else). The get_pending_int hunk (`GPTDWE & GPTDPF`) does not apply as-is, because the kb1200 driver never configures GPTDWE (no GPIO_INT_TRIG_WAKE handling), so masking with it would hide every pending interrupt.

evidence_refs.quote: Writing value 0 to the pin will set it to a low physical level.

title: The Ameba UART async driver reserves its devicetree DMA channels with a bare atomic_set_bit, so a channel that is already taken is never reported.
summary: In August 2026 the Realtek Bee UART driver (commit bd38a7e708) stopped reserving its RX/TX DMA channels by setting bits in the DMA controller's bitmap directly and switched to dma_request_channel() with a filter, adding per-direction NULL checks and failing init when a channel is already in use. The Ameba UART driver already has the per-direction NULL checks, so the single-direction crash the commit describes does not happen there, and its bitmap write does mark the channel for later dma_request_channel(dev, NULL) callers. It still uses atomic_set_bit, though, so a channel that another user already holds is shared without any error; the amebag2.dtsi defaults give every UART the same RX and TX channels, so a board that enables two async UARTs would get colliding DMA transfers instead of an init error. Porting needs adapting because the Ameba DMA filter expects the channel number rather than a BIT() mask, and this is a hardening gap rather than a crash, which is why confidence is medium.

fix.subject: drivers: serial: uart_bee: claim DMA channels via dma_request_channel

evidence: The uart_bee commit names three problems with reserving the devicetree DMA channels via atomic_set_bit: it "bypassed the public DMA API, never detected a channel that was already in use, and dereferenced dma_rx/dma_tx.dma_dev unconditionally", and replaces it with per-direction NULL checks plus dma_request_channel() that "returns an error when the channel is already taken". In uart_ameba_async_init the NULL-pointer crash is already handled differently (each atomic_set_bit sits inside its own `dma_dev != NULL` check, lines 1120 and 1125), and the cast still hits the right bitmap because dma_ameba_data has struct dma_context as its first member, with atomic pointing at channels_atomic. What is still missing is conflict detection: atomic_set_bit marks the channel taken even when it already was, so a second user of the same channel is never reported, and the amebag2.dtsi defaults put uart0 to uart3 all on RX channel 2 (and TX channel 3), so enabling two async UARTs makes them share channels silently; dma_ameba_configure and dma_ameba_start do not check for a busy channel either. The fix cannot be copied verbatim: the Ameba DMA chan_filter compares the filter value with the channel number (`channel == requested_channel`) instead of testing a BIT(ch) mask as the Bee filter does, so the Ameba version has to pass the channel number itself.
impact_note: With distinct devicetree channels the behaviour is unchanged; the missing check only turns a channel conflict from silent sharing into a reported init error.

title: The ADXL355 stream code keeps its cached FIFO-watermark interrupt flag when it drops an interrupt that arrives with no pending stream request, so a restarted stream can get stuck with no data.
summary: On 2026-08-03 the ADXL345 driver (commit c627cf26d123) began clearing data->fifo_watermark_irq when its status callback or interrupt handler finds no pending stream request, and in October 2026 the ADXL372 driver got the same change. The ADXL355 stream code, added in March 2026 with the same design, still just returns from adxl355_process_status1_cb and adxl355_stream_irq_handler when data->sqe is NULL, and still flushes the FIFO and reads STATUS in adxl355_submit_stream only when the cached flag changes. So after a stream is cancelled and the FIFO keeps filling, starting a new stream with the same watermark trigger skips the flush, the interrupt line can stay asserted, and the edge-triggered GPIO never fires, leaving the new stream without data. The fix is the same one-line reset in both early returns, using a field the driver already has. What the repository does not show directly is that the ADXL355 INT pin stays asserted while STATUS is unread; this is inferred from the sibling drivers' comments and the ADXL372 commit message.

fix.subject: drivers: sensor: adxl345: RTIO stream fix

evidence: The selected hunk adds data->fifo_watermark_irq = 0; to the data->sqe == NULL early return of adxl345_process_status1_cb (the same commit also adds it to adxl345_stream_irq_handler), and the message says "Because data->fifo_watermark_irq remain set, it was not possible to start new stream." adxl355_process_status1_cb (line 248) has the same pre-fix early return at line 259, adxl355_stream_irq_handler has another at line 377, and nothing else in the ADXL355 driver ever clears data->fifo_watermark_irq (declared in adxl355.h line 316). adxl355_submit_stream uses the same caching as ADXL345: only when fifo_watermark_irq != data->fifo_watermark_irq (line 59) does it flush the FIFO (line 70) and read ADXL355_STATUS (line 72), and it then arms the pin as GPIO_INT_EDGE_TO_ACTIVE (line 79), while the GPIO callback disables the pin before calling the stream handler (adxl355_trigger.c line 48). The mechanism is spelled out in the repository: the ADXL345 comment at adxl345_stream.c lines 16-17 says the FIFO keeps "the edge-triggered interrupt line asserted; clearing fifo_watermark_irq makes the next stream reconfigure and flush the FIFO", and the ADXL372 port of this fix (commit 384e1f966f) says that without it "INT1 stays high and the new stream never gets an edge" (adxl372_stream.c line 325 now has data->fifo_full_irq = 0;). The fix only uses a field the ADXL355 driver already has, so nothing it depends on is missing; confidence is medium because the stall also assumes the ADXL355 INT pin stays asserted while STATUS is unread, which the repository only suggests (the trigger thread comments "Clear the status" before reading ADXL355_STATUS, adxl355_trigger.c line 20).

title: The MAX30009 stream code keeps its cached FIFO-watermark interrupt flag when it drops an interrupt that arrives with no pending stream request, so a restarted stream can get stuck with no data.
summary: On 2026-08-03 the ADXL345 driver (commit c627cf26d123) began clearing data->fifo_watermark_irq when its status callback or interrupt handler finds no pending stream request, and in October 2026 the ADXL372 driver got the same change. The MAX30009 stream code, added on 2026-07-30 with the same design, still just returns from max30009_process_status1_cb and max30009_stream_irq_handler when data->sqe is NULL, and still flushes the FIFO and reads STATUS1 in max30009_submit_stream only when the cached flag changes. So after a stream is cancelled and the FIFO reaches its almost-full level, the dropped A_FULL interrupt stays pending in the unread STATUS1, a new stream with the same watermark trigger skips the flush and the STATUS1 read, and the edge-triggered GPIO may never fire again, leaving the new stream without data. The fix is the same one-line reset in both early returns, using a field the driver already has. What the repository does not show directly is that the MAX30009 INT pin stays asserted while A_FULL is pending; this is inferred from the driver's clear-on-read comment and the sibling drivers.

fix.subject: drivers: sensor: adxl345: RTIO stream fix

evidence: The selected hunk adds data->fifo_watermark_irq = 0; to the data->sqe == NULL early return of adxl345_process_status1_cb (the same commit also adds it to adxl345_stream_irq_handler), and the message says "Because data->fifo_watermark_irq remain set, it was not possible to start new stream." max30009_process_status1_cb (line 269) has the same pre-fix early return at line 280, max30009_stream_irq_handler has another at line 418, and nothing in the MAX30009 driver ever clears data->fifo_watermark_irq (declared in max30009.h line 512). max30009_submit_stream copies the ADXL345 caching: only when fifo_watermark_irq != data->fifo_watermark_irq (line 71) does it flush the FIFO (line 83) and read STATUS1 (line 85), and it then arms the pin as GPIO_INT_EDGE_TO_ACTIVE (line 92), while the GPIO callback disables the pin before calling the stream handler (max30009_trigger.c line 85). The driver itself describes STATUS1 as "the clear-on-read STATUS1 register" holding "pending events (A_FULL, FIFO_DATA_RDY)" (max30009.c lines 1092-1095), so an A_FULL interrupt dropped by the early return stays pending, and the ADXL345 comment (adxl345_stream.c lines 16-17) and the ADXL372 port of this fix (commit 384e1f966f: "INT1 stays high and the new stream never gets an edge") describe exactly this stall. The fix only uses a field the MAX30009 driver already has, so nothing it depends on is missing; confidence is medium because the repository does not state outright that the MAX30009 INT pin stays asserted while A_FULL is pending.

title: The i.MX IUART driver connects its interrupt using the raw devicetree interrupt cell instead of the multi-level encoded number, which is the wrong number for its node behind the i.MX8M audio DSP's IRQSTEER controller.
summary: In January 2024 the LPUART driver (commit c82789c5ff8f) switched IRQ_CONNECT from DT_INST_IRQ_BY_IDX(n, i, irq) to DT_INST_IRQN_BY_IDX(n, i), because for nodes behind a second-level interrupt controller the raw interrupt cell is no longer the Zephyr interrupt number. The IUART driver's MCUX_IUART_IRQ_INIT still passes the raw cell to IRQ_CONNECT and irq_enable. On the Cortex-M4/M7 and Cortex-A53 i.MX8M SoCs every IUART node sits directly under the NVIC or GIC, where both macros give the same value, so nothing changes there. The i.MX8MP audio DSP board, however, uses an IUART (uart4) behind IRQSTEER master0 as its console and shell UART with multi-level interrupts enabled, so in interrupt-driven mode the handler is registered under the un-encoded number. Because that node's interrupt number is explicitly a placeholder until UART interrupts are supported on the DSP, the fix mainly matters once real UART interrupts are wired up there.

fix.subject: drivers: serial: uart_mcux_lpuart: Switch to using DT_INST_IRQN_BY_IDX

changes.diff:
#ifdef CONFIG_UART_MCUX_LPUART_ISR_SUPPORT
 #define MCUX_LPUART_IRQ_INSTALL(n, i)					\
 	do {								\
-		IRQ_CONNECT(DT_INST_IRQ_BY_IDX(n, i, irq),		\
+		IRQ_CONNECT(DT_INST_IRQN_BY_IDX(n, i),			\
 			    DT_INST_IRQ_BY_IDX(n, i, priority),		\
 			    mcux_lpuart_isr, DEVICE_DT_INST_GET(n), 0);	\
 									\
changes.target_now:
280  
  281  #ifdef CONFIG_UART_INTERRUPT_DRIVEN
  282  #define MCUX_IUART_IRQ_INIT(n, i)					\
  283  	do {								\
  284> 		IRQ_CONNECT(DT_INST_IRQ_BY_IDX(n, i, irq),		\
  285  			    DT_INST_IRQ_BY_IDX(n, i, priority),		\
  286  			    mcux_iuart_isr, DEVICE_DT_INST_GET(n), 0);	\
  287  									\
  288  		irq_enable(DT_INST_IRQ_BY_IDX(n, i, irq));		\

evidence: The LPUART hunk replaces DT_INST_IRQ_BY_IDX(n, i, irq) with DT_INST_IRQN_BY_IDX(n, i) in IRQ_CONNECT, because, as the message says, with multi-level interrupts "using the generic DT_INST_IRQ_BY_IDX() to fetch the INTID is no longer an option as the queried INTID will be the one specified through the node's `interrupts` properties"; devicetree.h confirms that DT_IRQN_BY_IDX encodes the number through DT_MULTI_LEVEL_IRQN_INTERNAL when CONFIG_MULTI_LEVEL_INTERRUPTS is set and reduces to DT_IRQ_BY_IDX(node_id, idx, irq) only for a level-1 node (lines 3404 and 3460-3462). The IUART driver's MCUX_IUART_IRQ_INIT, compiled under CONFIG_UART_INTERRUPT_DRIVEN, still has the identical pre-fix IRQ_CONNECT(DT_INST_IRQ_BY_IDX(n, i, irq), ...) at line 284 (and irq_enable with the raw cell at line 288), and nothing else in the driver encodes the number. Most IUART nodes are level-1 (the Cortex-M i.MX8M dtsi inherits interrupt-parent = <&nvic> from armv7-m.dtsi, the A53 dtsi nodes use interrupt-parent = <&gic>), so there the two macros agree, but dts/xtensa/nxp/nxp_imx8m.dtsi puts IUART uart4 behind IRQSTEER master0 (lines 64, 69, 84), and the imx8mp_evk_mimx8ml8_adsp board uses it as console and shell UART with CONFIG_MULTI_LEVEL_INTERRUPTS=y (defconfig lines 21-22, board dts lines 19-20); since the IUART selects SERIAL_SUPPORT_INTERRUPT, an application that enables the shell gets the interrupt-driven serial backend by default, which selects UART_INTERRUPT_DRIVEN, and this code then registers the ISR for that node under the un-encoded number. Impact is light because the same node's comment says "This INTID is just a dummy" "until we can support UART interrupts" (lines 66-67), so UART interrupts on that DSP do not work either way today.

impact_note: Every IUART node on the Cortex-M and Cortex-A i.MX8M SoCs is wired directly to the NVIC or GIC, where both macros give the same number, and the only IUART node behind a second-level controller (the i.MX8M DSP uart4) has an interrupt number its own devicetree calls a placeholder until UART interrupts are supported, so no working configuration behaves differently today.

title: The STM32 I2C v2 RTIO driver does not hand an own-address match to target handling while its own controller START is still pending, so the target transfer is not serviced and the bus can hang.
summary: Commit dd9b1122e1 (2026-04-29) changed the non-RTIO STM32 I2C v2 driver so that an own-address match (ADDR) seen while the controller is marked active aborts the pending controller START and switches to target handling; follow-up 879678acbb for the same issue #99074 refined it, and neither touched the RTIO driver. i2c_stm32_v2_rtio.c, which drives the same v2 block, still sets controller_active before generating START, keeps the ADDR interrupt enabled while a target is registered, and its event ISR only goes to target handling when controller_active is false, while its controller path never checks or clears ADDR. If another controller on the bus addresses this device while its own transfer is waiting to start, the target callbacks do not run and ADDR stays pending, which per the commit message 'may leave the bus stuck'. The port has to be adapted because the RTIO data structure has no current.is_arlo or device_sync_sem, so the aborted request must be completed through the RTIO completion path. This is from reading the code only; the race needs a multi-controller bus with a registered target and has not been reproduced.

fix.subject: drivers: i2c: stm32_v2: abort pending controller START on ADDR

evidence: Of the three hunks, the first two only split i2c_stm32_target_event() into i2c_stm32_target_cfg_get() and i2c_stm32_target_addr_setup() (refactoring in support of the fix); the third is the behavioural change: with a target attached, if controller_active is set and ISR shows ADDR, abort the pending controller START and run target address handling, because 'controller mode may mark itself active before START is actually issued' and otherwise 'target IRQ handling can be blocked, which may leave the bus stuck'. i2c_stm32_v2_rtio.c is built for the same v2 block (CMakeLists line 128) and has the same pre-fix logic: i2c_stm32_msg_start() sets controller_active at line 692 before LL_I2C_GenerateStartCondition() at line 714, target registration enables the ADDR interrupt at line 394, and i2c_stm32_event() still routes to target handling only when !controller_active (line 497). Its controller path (TXIS/RXNE, NACK, STOP, TC/TCR) never reads or clears ADDR, which is handled only inside i2c_stm32_target_event() (line 291), and neither this file nor the RTIO start path in i2c_stm32_rtio.c waits for BUSY or otherwise checks for an own-address match. The flags the fix needs are already used by this driver (LL_I2C_IsActiveFlag_ADDR, LL_I2C_ClearFlag_ADDR), the fix and its follow-ups (879678acbb, d2d09bde31, a1609f6a45) only changed i2c_stm32_v2.c, and no later commit to the RTIO file covers this case.

title: The Broadcom PAX v1 DMA driver still starts at the generic DMA init priority, before the PCIe endpoint it requires, so its init fails or the default init-priority check rejects the build.
summary: In July 2023 the PAX v2 DMA driver got its own init priority symbol (default 51) so that it starts after the iProc PCIe endpoint driver it depends on through the pcie-ep phandle. The PAX v1 driver, which had the same code at that time, still uses CONFIG_DMA_INIT_PRIORITY (default 40) while the PCIe endpoint driver starts at 50, and its init function returns -ENODEV when the endpoint is not yet initialized. On a board that uses the v1 compatible, the default build-time priority check would reject the build, and with that check off the DMA device would fail to initialize at boot. The port is the same Kconfig symbol under a v1 name used in v1's device definition. No in-tree devicetree enables brcm,iproc-pax-dma-v1, so only out-of-tree boards are affected, which is why confidence is medium.

fix.subject: dma: iproc_pax_v2: delay initialization after pcie

changes.diff:
&pax_dma_data,
 		    &pax_dma_cfg,
 		    POST_KERNEL,
-		    CONFIG_DMA_INIT_PRIORITY,
+		    CONFIG_DMA_IPROC_PAX_V2_INIT_PRIORITY,
 		    &pax_dma_driver_api);
changes.target_now:
986  		    NULL,
  987  		    &pax_dma_data,
  988  		    &pax_dma_cfg,
  989  		    POST_KERNEL,
  990> 		    CONFIG_DMA_INIT_PRIORITY,
  991  		    &pax_dma_driver_api);
  992

evidence: The hunk moves the PAX v2 DMA device from CONFIG_DMA_INIT_PRIORITY to a new CONFIG_DMA_IPROC_PAX_V2_INIT_PRIORITY (default 51) because, in the commit message's words, "The Broadcom pcie setup has a devicetree dependency" and the build reported "/pcie/paxdma@4e100800 POST_KERNEL 40 < /pcie/pcie@4e100000 POST_KERNEL 50"; at the fix's parent v1 and v2 had identical code here. dma_iproc_pax_v1.c still has the pre-fix logic: its config takes pcie_dev from the required pcie-ep phandle (line 981), dma_iproc_pax_init returns -ENODEV when device_is_ready(cfg->pcie_dev) is false (lines 594-596), and the device is defined at POST_KERNEL with CONFIG_DMA_INIT_PRIORITY (line 990), whose default is KERNEL_INIT_PRIORITY_DEFAULT = 40. The only PCIe endpoint driver, pcie_ep_iproc.c (compatible brcm_iproc_pcie_ep, which DMA_IPROC_PAX pairs with via select PCIE_ENDPOINT), initializes at CONFIG_KERNEL_INIT_PRIORITY_DEVICE = 50, and device_is_ready() just returns dev->state->initialized, so with default settings the v1 DMA runs its init before its endpoint and fails; with CONFIG_CHECK_INIT_PRIORITIES (default y) the build is rejected instead. Kconfig.iproc_pax adds a priority symbol only for DMA_IPROC_PAX_V2 and nothing else in the v1 driver orders it after the endpoint. Caveat that lowers confidence: no in-tree devicetree uses brcm,iproc-pax-dma-v1 (the only PAX DMA node, in viper-common.dtsi, is v2), so only out-of-tree boards would hit this.

title: The MAX32 I3C controller fails to initialize when the devicetree omits i2c-scl-hz or i3c-scl-hz, because init never fills in default SCL rates.
summary: In 2024 the NXP MCUX I3C driver was fixed to fill in default I2C and I3C SCL rates in its init function when the devicetree leaves them out, because its configure function rejects a zero rate and init otherwise failed. The MAX32 I3C driver, added in 2025, has the same structure: the rates come from DT_INST_PROP_OR(..., 0), max32_i3c_configure returns -EINVAL for a zero rate, and max32_i3c_init calls it without setting any defaults. On a board or overlay that enables the MAX32 I3C controller without both rate properties, which the binding allows and says should mean the controller default, the controller fails to initialize and the bus is unusable. The NXP HAL default-config call does not exist for MAX32 and the MAX32 HAL is not in this repository, so the port has to choose default rates itself. The in-tree max32657evkit board sets both properties, so it is not affected today.

fix.subject: driver: i3c: fixing i3c init error

evidence: The hunk makes mcux_i3c_init fill ctrl_config->scl.i2c and scl.i3c with HAL defaults when they are 0, before calling the configure function, because (commit message) "i3c config need has i2x/i3c baudrate configured first. so in i3c init we shall set the baudrate first"; the mcux configure function returns -EINVAL when either rate is 0, so without it the controller failed to initialize whenever the devicetree left the rates out. max32_i3c_init has the same pre-fix sequence: after k_mutex_init/k_condvar_init (lines 1816-1817) it goes straight to max32_i3c_configure (line 1825) and returns -EINVAL on failure (line 1827), while max32_i3c_configure rejects a zero scl.i2c or scl.i3c with -EINVAL (lines 1654-1655), and the instance macro fills both from DT_INST_PROP_OR(..., 0) (lines 2005-2006). Neither the adi,max32-i3c binding nor i3c-controller.yaml gives these properties a default, and i3c-controller.yaml says that when i3c-scl-hz is undefined the driver should "use the controller default", so omitting them is a valid devicetree that the MAX32 driver turns into an init failure; nothing else in i3c_max32.c writes scl.i2c or scl.i3c. The fix's I3C_MasterGetDefaultConfig is an NXP HAL call and the MAX32 HAL is not in this repository, so a port must pick its own default rates (adapt). The only in-tree user, max32657evkit, sets both i2c-scl-hz and i3c-scl-hz, so the failure only shows on boards or overlays that omit them, which is why confidence is medium.

evidence_refs.quote: /* Currently can only act as primary controller. */
use the controller default or as specified by the I3C specification.

title: The Egis ET171 SPI driver cuts full-duplex transfers down to the shorter of the TX and RX lengths, a bug already fixed in the Andes ATCSPI200 driver it was copied from.
summary: The Andes ATCSPI200 SPI driver was fixed in commit f817f62021 (merged 2025-07-31): full-duplex transfers are now sized by MAX of the TX and RX lengths, with exact TX/RX frame counters so the shorter side is padded with dummy frames, because the IP needs equal write and read counts; the same commit also corrected how chained DMA blocks are counted. The Egis ET171 driver, whose binding and Kconfig say it is based on the ATCSPI200, was added on 2025-08-16 with the older code: transceive() still uses MIN(rx_len, tx_len), programs that one count into both transfer counters, and finishes the transaction at the END interrupt. A call such as a register-address write followed by a longer read therefore clocks only the shorter length and returns success, leaving the rest of the RX buffer unfilled (or the extra TX bytes unsent), and the DMA reload callbacks and chained block count still follow the old logic. Porting means reworking the interrupt handler and DMA loaders around the counters, not only changing MIN to MAX; note that at the pinned commit no in-tree devicetree defines an egis,et171-spi node, so the driver only runs when a board or overlay adds one.

fix.subject: drivers: spi: atcspi200: Fix the bug for inconsistent TX/RX lengths.

changes.diff:
.channel_direction = ANDES_DMA_CONFIG_DIRECTION(		\
 				     DMA_CHANNEL_CONFIG(index, dir)),		\
 		.complete_callback_en = 0,					\
-		.error_callback_dis = 0,					\
+		.error_callback_en = 0,						\
 		.source_data_size =						\
 			ANDES_DMA_CONFIG_##src_dev##_DATA_SIZE(			\
 					DMA_CHANNEL_CONFIG(index, dir)		\
changes.target_now:
1267  			.dma_slot = DT_INST_DMAS_CELL_BY_NAME(index, dir, slot),                   \
 1268  			.channel_direction =                                                       \
 1269  				EGIS_DMA_CONFIG_DIRECTION(DMA_CHANNEL_CONFIG(index, dir)),        \
 1270  			.complete_callback_en = 0,                                                 \
 1271> 			.error_callback_dis = 0,                                                   \
 1272  			.source_data_size = EGIS_DMA_CONFIG_##src_dev##_DATA_SIZE(                \
 1273  				DMA_CHANNEL_CONFIG(index, dir)),                                   \
 1274  			.dest_data_size = EGIS_DMA_CONFIG_##dest_dev##_DATA_SIZE(                 \
 1275  				DMA_CHANNEL_CONFIG(index, dir)),                                   \

evidence: The listed hunks are the core of the ATCSPI200 fix: transceive() now sizes a full-duplex transfer with MAX(rx_len, tx_len) instead of MIN, and the DMA callbacks decide whether to reload from exact remaining frame counters (data->rx_cnt/tx_cnt) instead of spi_context_rx_on/tx_on, because, as the commit message says, "the transmission and reception counts must be consistent. If there is a mismatch in length, dummy data needs to be transmitted or received"; the block_idx-to-block_count resets in the error and END paths belong to the same DMA chain rework. spi_egis_et171.c is a copy of the pre-fix driver for the same IP (its binding says "based on the Andes ATCSPI200 architecture", and its header has the same register map and TRNS_MODE_WRITE_READ): transceive() still sets chunk_len = MIN(rx_len, tx_len) (line 681), spi_transfer() and spi_transfer_dma() write that one count to both SPI_WR_TRANS_CNT and SPI_RD_TRANS_CNT, the IRQ handler stops feeding TX once tx_cnt reaches chunk_len and calls spi_context_complete on the END interrupt, and dma_rx_callback/dma_tx_callback still test spi_context_rx_on/tx_on (lines 320 and 347). So any full-duplex call whose TX and RX totals differ (for example a 1-byte command followed by a longer read) clocks only the shorter length and returns success with the rest of the buffers never transferred, although spi.h says CS is held until all buffers in the provided buf sets have been transferred. Nothing in spi_egis_et171.c pads or splits such transfers, the fix needs only driver-local counters plus register macros and spi_context helpers that the ET171 side already has, and the chained-DMA line block_count = ctx->tx_count (line 434) that the same commit replaced is also still there (the ATCDMACx00 driver follows a chain only when block_count > 1). The ET171 file was reorganised (DMA block helper functions, DCACHE re-alignment of RX buffers), so the change has to be rewritten rather than copied; the commit's other edits that roll back API updates (DEVICE_API, error_callback_dis, SPI_DEVICE_DT_INST_DEFINE) are not part of the fix, since the fixed driver uses all three again today (lines 730, 897 and 972).

title: The FXLS8974 accelerometer driver's SPI burst read skips one byte too many, so SPI samples are read one register late.
summary: On 2026-09-24 the fxos8700 driver fixed its SPI burst read to skip only the 2-byte address phase instead of 3 bytes, matching its own single-byte read and write paths. fxls8974_read_spi() is a line-for-line copy of the old fxos8700 code and still discards 3 bytes, while the same driver's byte read takes the register value from the 3rd byte and its init relies on that to check WHOAMI and CTRL_REG4. With the sensor on SPI, sample_fetch's burst read of OUT_X_LSB onward therefore returns data starting one register later, so X, Y and Z are built from the wrong bytes (the I2C path is not affected). The fxos8700 change can be applied with only the names changed.

fix.subject: drivers: sensor: fxos8700: fix off-by-one in SPI burst read

evidence: The fxos8700 commit says "The SPI burst read discarded 3 leading bytes, but the device's address phase is only 2 bytes long, so every sample was shifted by one register. Skip 2 bytes instead, matching the single-byte read and write paths." fxls8974_read_spi() in fxls8974.c is the same pre-fix code line for line (lines 41-47): it sends reg_buf[3] = { DIR_READ(reg), ADDR_7(reg), 0 } and uses that 3-byte buffer as the first RX entry, so the caller's data starts on the 4th byte. The same file's single-byte paths use a 2-byte address phase, exactly like fxos8700: fxls8974_byte_read_spi() clocks 3 bytes and returns data[2] (line 62) and fxls8974_byte_write_spi() sends the value as the 3rd byte (line 71); fxls8974_init() depends on that byte read to accept the WHOAMI value and to verify CTRL_REG4 after writing it (lines 517 and 544-549), so on a working SPI part the burst read is one register late. That burst read is what fxls8974_sample_fetch() uses for all accelerometer axes from FXLS8974_REG_OUTXLSB (line 272), so every SPI sample would be assembled from the wrong registers; nothing else in the driver compensates, and the fix uses only spi_buf/spi_buf_set and the DIR_READ/ADDR_7 macros that fxls8974.c already defines.

evidence_refs.quote: /* The address phase is 2 bytes; data starts on the 3rd byte. */

title: adxl367_fifo_flush_rtio() uses RTIO submission entries without checking that they were acquired, so running out of them dereferences NULL in the FIFO flush path.
summary: Commit 2abd8f6782 (2026-08-20) fixed max30009_flush_rtio(): when it could not acquire RTIO submission entries it reported the error on data->sqe, which is already NULL at that point, and crashed; it now drops the partially acquired entries with rtio_sqe_drop_all(), re-enables the interrupt and returns. The corresponding adxl367_fifo_flush_rtio() runs in the same situation (the DROP branch, after data->sqe has been cleared) but does not check rtio_sqe_acquire() at all: it takes five entries from an 8-entry pool and writes through each pointer straight away. If the pool is exhausted, adxl367 crashes with a NULL dereference instead of logging the failure, dropping the partial entries and re-enabling its interrupt. The patch cannot be copied line for line: adxl367 first needs the NULL checks, then the same rtio_sqe_drop_all() error path. The root cause is not identical to max30009 (no check at all, rather than a wrong pointer inside the check), and pool exhaustion is an uncommon condition, so a human should confirm that this counts as the same problem.

fix.subject: drivers: sensor: max30009: fix NULL deref in flush_rtio error path

evidence: The hunk is a real fix: per the commit message, max30009_flush_rtio() runs only after the streaming request 'was already completed with rtio_iodev_sqe_ok and data->sqe was set to NULL', so its SQE-acquire-failure branch 'dereferenced NULL'; the fix drops the partially acquired SQEs with rtio_sqe_drop_all() instead. The corresponding adxl367_fifo_flush_rtio() (line 36) is called in the same situation, from the SENSOR_STREAM_DATA_DROP branch of adxl367_process_status_cb() after 'data->sqe = NULL;' (lines 507 and 522-524). It never checks rtio_sqe_acquire() for NULL: it acquires five SQEs (lines 44, 49, 55, 66, 67) from an 8-entry pool (adxl367.c line 1182) and passes each straight to rtio_sqe_prep_tiny_write() or rtio_sqe_prep_callback() (lines 47 and 72), while rtio.h documents that rtio_sqe_acquire() returns NULL when no SQE is available and rtio_sqe_prep_tiny_write() starts with memset(sqe, 0, ...) (sqe.h line 641). So when the SQE pool is exhausted, adxl367 ends the same way max30009 did before the fix, with a NULL dereference in the flush path; the cause differs (no check at all, rather than a NULL request passed to rtio_iodev_sqe_err()), which is why confidence is medium and the port has to be adapted. Nothing ties the fix to hardware or configuration: both drivers use the same RTIO API, and the fix only changes how an SQE shortage is handled.
